Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. - **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). - The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 719
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/719
- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225 all sat BLOCKED with green latches and zero failing checks — 'Quality gate' simply absent on heads. Manual ci.yml dispatches unblocked them.

Edge cases:
1. The commit message is interpolated into `git commit -m "` + commitMsg + `"` — shell double-quote. If commitMsg contains a `"` character or `$`/backtick, this is command injection. But that's pre-existing behavior (template-driven), not introduced here. Stripping tokens doesn't make it worse. Could note as pre-existing.

2. `stripCiSkipTokens` doesn't handle `[skip-ci]` etc.? Regex `skip[\s-]?ci` handles `skip ci`, `skip-ci`, `skipci`. GitHub only honors the spaced forms actually? Let me recall: GitHub docs say the skip directive can be anywhere? Historically `[skip ci]` needed brackets... Actually the docs state: "you can skip workflow runs triggered by push and pull_request events by including a command in your commit message". The commands are `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`. Some sources say any of these strings without brackets also work. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3

- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225 all sat BLOCKED with green latches and zero failing checks — 'Quality gate' simply absent on heads. Manual ci.yml dispatches unblocked them.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 719
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/719
- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225 all sat BLOCKED with green latches and zero failing checks — 'Quality gate' simply absent on heads. Manual ci.yml dispatches unblocked them.

GitHub docs list: `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]` — the regex covers those with optional space or hyphen separators, case-insensitive. Good.

Edge cases:
1. The commit message is interpolated into `git commit -m "` + commitMsg + `"` — shell double-quote. If commitMsg contains a `"` character or `$`/backtick, this is command injection. But that's pre-existing behavior (template-driven), not introduced here. Stripping tokens doesn't make it worse. Could note as pre-existing.

2. `stripCiSkipTokens` doesn't handle `[skip-ci]` etc.? Regex `skip[\s-]?ci` handles `skip ci`, `skip-ci`, `skipci`. GitHub only honors the spaced forms actually? GitHub docs: the strings "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — case-insensitive, must be within brackets? Actually GitHub's rule: if commit message contains `[skip ci]` or `[ci skip]` etc. I believe the directive must be in brackets? Actually per GitHub docs, "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — these can appear anywhere in the commit message? Let me recall: GitHub docs say the skip directive can be anywhere? Historically `[skip ci]` needed brackets... Actually the docs state: "you can skip workflow runs triggered by push and pull_request events by including a command in your commit message". The commands are `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`. Some sources say any of these strings without brackets also work. To be safe the fix handles bracketed forms, which is what templates carry. Fine.

3. Edge: token like `[skipped ci]`? regex requires exact token inside brackets; `[skip ci extra]`? GitHub wouldn't skip that anyway. Fine.

4. Whitespace collapse regex only collapses spaces/tabs, not newlines — commit message from template is single-line anyway (used with -m). Fine.

5. If stripping leaves empty message, `git commit -m ""` — edge: template is entirely `[skip ci]`. Unlikely; ticketKey almost always in template. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion? Maybe suggestion.

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 719
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/719
- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

GitHub docs list: `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]` — the regex covers those with optional space or hyphen separators, case-insensitive. Good.

Edge cases:
1. The commit message is interpolated into `git commit -m "` + commitMsg + `"` — shell double-quote. If commitMsg contains a `"` character or `$`/backtick, this is command injection. But that's pre-existing behavior (template-driven), not introduced here. Stripping tokens doesn't make it worse. Could note as pre-existing.

2. `stripCiSkipTokens` doesn't handle `[skip-ci]` etc.? Regex `skip[\s-]?ci` handles `skip ci`, `skip-ci`, `skipci`. GitHub only honors the spaced forms actually? GitHub docs: the strings "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — case-insensitive, must be within brackets? Actually GitHub's rule: if commit message contains `[skip ci]` or `[ci skip]` etc. I believe the directive must be in brackets? Actually per GitHub docs, "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — these can appear anywhere in the commit message? Let me recall: GitHub docs say the skip directive can be anywhere? Historically `[skip ci]` needed brackets... Actually the docs state: "you can skip workflow runs triggered by push and pull_request events by including a command in your commit message". The commands are `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`. Some sources say any of these strings without brackets also work. To be safe the fix handles bracketed forms, which is what templates carry. Fine.

3. Edge: token like `[skipped ci]`? regex requires exact token inside brackets; `[skip ci extra]`? GitHub wouldn't skip that anyway. Fine.

4. Whitespace collapse regex only collapses spaces/tabs, not newlines — commit message from template is single-line anyway (used with -m). Fine.

5. If stripping leaves empty message, `git commit -m ""` — edge: template is entirely `[skip ci]`. Unlikely; ticketKey almost always in template. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion? Maybe suggestion.

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 719
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/719
- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225 all sat BLOCKED with green latches and zero failing checks — 'Quality gate' simply absent on heads. Manual ci.yml dispatches unblocked them.

GitHub docs list: `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]` — the regex covers those with optional space or hyphen separators, case-insensitive. Good.

Edge cases:
1. The commit message is interpolated into `git commit -m "` + commitMsg + `"` — shell double-quote. If commitMsg contains a `"` character or `$`/backtick, this is command injection. But that's pre-existing behavior (template-driven), not introduced here. Stripping tokens doesn't make it worse. Could note as pre-existing.

2. `stripCiSkipTokens` doesn't handle `[skip-ci]` etc.? Regex `skip[\s-]?ci` handles `skip ci`, `skip-ci`, `skipci`. GitHub only honors the spaced forms actually? GitHub docs: the strings "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — case-insensitive, must be within brackets? Actually GitHub's rule: if commit message contains `[skip ci]` or `[ci skip]` etc. I believe the directive must be in brackets? Actually per GitHub docs, "skip ci", "ci skip", "no ci", "skip actions", "actions skip" — these can appear anywhere in the commit message? Let me recall: GitHub docs say the skip directive can be anywhere? Historically `[skip ci]` needed brackets... Actually the docs state: "you can skip workflow runs triggered by push and pull_request events by including a command in your commit message". The commands are `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`. Some sources say any of these strings without brackets also work. To be safe the fix handles bracketed forms, which is what templates carry. Fine.

3. Edge: token like `[skipped ci]`? regex requires exact token inside brackets; `[skip ci extra]`? GitHub wouldn't skip that anyway. Fine.

4. Whitespace collapse regex only collapses spaces/tabs, not newlines — commit message from template is single-line anyway (used with -m). Fine.

# Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 719
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/719
- **Title**: gh-711 conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-711` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +104
- **Deletions**: -1
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). At minimum document the dependency.

## Evidence

fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225 all sat BLOCKED with green latches and zero failing checks — 'Quality gate' simply absent on heads. Manual ci.yml dispatches unblocked them.

Edge cases:
1. The commit message is interpolated into `git commit -m "` + commitMsg + `"` — shell double-quote. If commitMsg contains a `"` character or `$`/backtick, this is command injection. But that's pre-existing behavior (template-driven), not introduced here. Stripping tokens doesn't make it worse. Could note as pre-existing.

2. `stripCiSkipTokens` doesn't handle `[skip-ci]` etc.? Regex `skip[\s-]?ci` handles `skip ci`, `skip-ci`, `skipci`. GitHub only honors the spaced forms actually? Actually the docs state: "you can skip workflow runs triggered by push and pull_request events by including a command in your commit message". The commands are `[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`. Some sources say any of these strings without brackets also work. # Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:35:56Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.

Skip instructions only apply to the workflow run(s) that would be triggered by the commit that contains the skip instructions. You can also disable a workflow from running. For more information, see [Disabling and enabling a workflow](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `skip-checks` trailer is not stripped — the "never skip CI" invariant has a hole**

GitHub honors two skip mechanisms (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/skip-workflow-runs):

1. the bracketed directives this regex strips — covered ✅
2. a `skip-checks: true` / `skip-checks:true` **commit-message trailer** — **not covered** ❌

The docblock promises "A rework push exists precisely to re-validate the PR, so the directive is stripped here", but a project template like `{ticketKey} Rework: address PR review comments\n\nskip-checks: true` would still suppress CI and re-create the exact gh-711 starvation this PR fixes. Since this function is now the single choke point guaranteeing the invariant, consider stripping the trailer form too, e.g. append:

```javascript
.replace(/\nskip-checks:\s?true\s*$/i, '')
```

(Placement matters: the trailer must be at the end of the message per GitHub's parsing, so anchoring the strip at end-of-string avoids eating legitimate mid-message text.)

💡 **SUGGESTION: escape double quotes in the commit message (pre-existing, now on a touched line)**

`commitMsg` is interpolated into a double-quoted shell string without escaping:

```javascript
cmd('git commit -m "' + commitMsg + '"');
```

A rework template containing a `"` (e.g. `Rework: addressed "nit" comments`) breaks the command or worse. The sibling commit sites already escape — `js/postTestReworkChanges.js` and `js/storyTestAutomationRework.js` both use `.replace(/"/g, '\\"')`. Cheap one-liner to match them here:

```javascript
cmd('git commit -m "' + commitMsg.replace(/"/g, '\\"') + '"');
```

Pre-existing behavior, so not blocking — but this is the one line the PR touches, so it's the natural place to align.

## PR Description

### Root Cause
- Rework legs built the commit message verbatim from the project-configured `formats.commitMessage.rework` template. Where that template carries a CI-skip directive (`[skip ci]`), the rework push on a validation-bound PR branch triggered no CI — the ruleset-required 'Quality gate' check never registered on the new head, leaving `mergeStateStatus` BLOCKED with green latches (live fa #1212/#1217/#1221/#1222/#1223/#1225, 2026-10-04).
- The validate-fresh/validate-armed arm only dispatches CI at the serial slot, so approved PRs waited until a manual `ci.yml` dispatch.

### Fix
- `js/pushReworkChanges.js`: added `stripCiSkipTokens()` and applied it at the single rework commit site in `commitAndPush()` — GitHub skip directives (`[skip ci]`, `[ci skip]`, `[no ci]`, `[skip actions]`, `[actions skip]`) are removed case-insensitively regardless of the configured template. A rework push exists to re-validate the PR, so it must never skip CI.
- `docs/machine-factory-integration.md`: documented the dependency in §9 (CI cost policy) — validation-bound branches must never carry CI-skip directives; keep them only on branches no ruleset requires checks on (e.g. factory-data).

### Test Coverage
- RED first: 2 new reproduction tests in `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` (template with `[skip ci]`; upper-case `[SKIP CI]`) — both FAILED before the fix.
- GREEN: `run_pushReworkChanges.json` — 44 passed, 0 failed.
- Full suite: `run_all.json` — 1485 passed, 0 failed, no regressions.

### Notes
- `js/factoryState.js` `[skip ci]` publishes (gh-676) intentionally untouched — the factory-data branch has no required checks.
- Test-automation rework legs (`postTestReworkResults.js`, `storyTestAutomationRework.js`) use their own `testRework` template and were not part of the gh-711 evidence; if their templates ever gain a skip directive, the same strip should be applied there.
- Behavior change to flag for consumers: a project that deliberately set `[skip ci]` in its rework template will now see CI run on rework pushes — that is the intended fix (option (a) from the ticket).

# gh-711: conveyor gap: rework pushes with [skip ci] starve the required Quality gate check

## Description

## Symptom (live, fa queue 2026-10-04)

The fa ruleset main-protection requires the 'Quality gate' check (aggregate job of dispatch-only ci.yml). Rework legs push fixes with [skip ci] in the commit message — correct for avoiding CI noise — but the required check never registers on the new head, so mergeStateStatus stays BLOCKED even after the rework succeeds and threads resolve.

## Options

(a) Rework pushes on validation-bound branches should omit [skip ci]; or (b) the validate-fresh/validate-armed rules should explicitly dispatch ci.yml when the head lacks the required check (they already do — but the arm only comes at the serial slot, so approved PRs wait). # Skipping workflow runs

You can skip workflow runs triggered by the `push` and `pull_request` events by including a command in your commit message.

Copy markdown

Note

 If a workflow is skipped due to [path filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpushpull_requestpull_request_targetpathspaths-ignore), [branch filtering](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#onpull_requestpull_request_targetbranchesbranches-ignore) or a commit message (see below), then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a "Pending" state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful will be blocked from merging.

Workflows that would otherwise be triggered using `on: push` or `on: pull_request` won't be triggered if you add any of the following strings to the commit message in a push, or the HEAD commit of a pull request:

- `[skip ci]`
- `[ci skip]`
- `[no ci]`
- `[skip actions]`
- `[actions skip]`

Alternatively, you can add a `skip-checks` trailer to your commit message. The trailers section should be included at the end of your commit message and be preceded by two empty lines. If you already have other trailers in your commit message, `skip-checks` should be last. You can use either of the following:

- `skip-checks:true`
- `skip-checks: true`

By default, Git automatically removes consecutive newlines. To leave the commit message exactly as you entered it, use the `--cleanup=verbatim` option on your commit. For more information, see [`--cleanup=<mode>`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit#Documentation/git-commit.txt---cleanupltmodegt) in the Git documentation.

You won't be able to merge the pull request if your repository is configured to require specific checks to pass first. To allow the pull request to be merged you can push a new commit to the pull request without the skip instruction in the commit message.

Note

 Skip instructions only apply to the `push` and `pull_request` events. For example, adding `[skip ci]` to a commit message won't stop a workflow that's triggered `on: pull_request_target` from running.
